meta.title: Weekly cybersecurity threat-intel brief
meta.bottom_line: Patch Acme Gateway now and check for web shells: attackers used CVE-2026-120118 for four days before the advisory. Rotate npm tokens if your builds ran after 2 November.
meta.methodology: We read posts and videos from a fixed list of vendor, media and independent accounts for the IST week. We grouped stories into themes and ranked them by distinct accounts. We clustered comments on the top themes and labelled their sentiment.

method_steps.title: Collect
method_steps.detail: Read every post from the tracked X accounts and every video from the tracked YouTube channels in the IST week.

method_steps.title: Group
method_steps.detail: Group posts that tell the same story into one theme.

method_steps.title: Rank
method_steps.detail: Rank themes by the number of distinct accounts that covered them. Keep themes with at least 5.

method_steps.title: Read the comments
method_steps.detail: Cluster replies and quotes on the key posts and label each comment's sentiment.

themes.name: Acme Gateway pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-120118) exploited against edge appliances

references.title: Web shells on Acme Gateway appliances

themes.why_line: A pre-auth flaw in an internet-facing gateway is being used to plant web shells before most teams patched.
themes.summary: Acme confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-120118, a pre-authentication flaw in the Acme Gateway management portal. Two incident-response firms reported web shells on appliances from 26 October, four days before the advisory. A second flaw, CVE-2026-120119, lets an authenticated user read session secrets. The same release fixes it.
themes.why: Edge appliances sit outside most endpoint tools, so a gateway shell can go unseen while attackers harvest VPN sessions. Exploitation started before the advisory, so patching alone does not prove the box is clean.
actions: Upgrade Acme Gateway to 9.4.2 or later.
Rotate session secrets and VPN certificates after patching.
Hunt for PHP files in /var/tmp/portal newer than the last upgrade.

clusters.label: Patch status and the gap before the fix

samples.text: Patched within the hour, but the advisory came out four days after the first web shells. That gap is the story.
9.4.2 breaks SAML for us. Rolling back is not an option, so we are blocking the endpoint at the WAF for now.

clusters.label: Hunting for web shells on appliances

samples.text: Look in /var/tmp/portal for .php files newer than the last upgrade.

cve_details.basis: Fixed in the same release. No report of exploitation yet (Northwind News)

themes.name: Self-spreading npm worm steals CI tokens and publishes poisoned releases
themes.why_line: Stolen publish tokens let the worm push releases that look legitimate to anyone who installs them.
themes.summary: A malicious npm package steals CI tokens from builds. It then uses each token to publish poisoned versions of the packages it can reach. Researchers have counted 14 affected versions so far. Registry staff have removed the known versions and revoked the exposed tokens.
themes.why: Any build that installed an affected version may have leaked its publish token, which turns one infection into many. Lockfiles pinned before 2 November are safe.
actions: Check lockfiles for the 14 published versions.
Rotate npm and CI tokens used since 2 November.

samples.text: Short-lived publish tokens would have stopped this. Most teams still use one token for everything.

themes.name: AI-written phishing kits target Contoso 365 tenants
themes.why_line: Unique lures per tenant get past template filters. The token-theft proxy behind them has not changed.
themes.summary: Phishing kits sold on two forums now generate a unique lure for each Contoso 365 tenant they target. The kits still route victims through the same adversary-in-the-middle proxy to steal session tokens.
themes.why: Filters that match known templates miss these lures, but phishing-resistant sign-in still stops the token theft.
actions: Move admins to passkeys or FIDO2 keys.
Alert on sign-ins from the known proxy ranges.

clusters.label: Filters cannot keep up with unique lures

samples.text: Every message is different, so the old hash and template rules are useless.
Passkeys make the proxy pointless. Roll them out to admins first.
